_doc: Per-cell corrections + accept-list for shp_history.json. Applied by fetch_shareholding.py
(apply_cell_fix) on every run, AFTER the fetch loop — never edit shp_history.json directly
(CLAUDE.md rule 5, runbook §22g). Idempotent; re-running a backfill cannot re-poison a fixed cell.
fix.<SYM>.<QE> = the ordinary-equity pattern, replacing a filing that describes something else.
cell = [prom, fii, dii, mf, ins, sub-date, nsh]  (same shape as shp_history)
src  = system:document that the corrected numbers were parsed from
was  = the wrong cell being replaced, kept so the override is auditable and self-checking:
if the stored cell no longer matches `was`, apply_cell_fix warns instead of silently
overwriting whatever is there now.
accept.<SYM>.<QE> = a shareholder-count collapse that is REAL (post-insolvency capital
reduction, pre-IPO pattern, ...). Exempts the cell from the write-time nsh scale gate so a
--reparse cannot punch a hole in correct data. See runbook §22g for how each was adjudicated.

2026-09-22 (§142e): fix.<SYM>.<DATE> with a NON-quarter-end DATE names an EVENT row in scripts/shp_events.json (apply_cell_fix_events); quarter-end keys keep naming shp_history cells. A `superseded` field keeps the earlier entry this one chains from.

2026-09-22 (§142g): `retired` holds entries whose stored cell was neither the fix nor its `was` (orphans). Rule adopted: VALUES AND DATE COME FROM THE SAME DOCUMENT, and the document that serves a quarter is the EARLIEST PUBLIC filing (the original); a revision replaces it only when its own gated publication date falls in the same visibility window (same-day re-filing). Late revisions are recorded here, never served at the original's date.

2026-09-22 (§142i): dark-window repair — 747 rows (as-on >= Sep-2025) re-dated by the fetcher to a later re-publication restored to BSE's ORIGINAL filing (values + gated date from that one document); the fetcher no longer re-dates or overwrites a stored row on a re-filing.

2026-09-22 (§142j, USER RULE): a quarter's row keeps the ORIGINAL filing's gated date but serves the LATEST re-filing's values (corrections are small and must be reflected). Supersedes the §142g 'original values' reading; `retired` entries whose revision values now serve were re-activated with the original date.

2026-09-22 (§142k, option C): the store row is the ORIGINAL filing; re-filings live in scripts/shp_revisions.json with their own gated dates (engine serves each from its date, stock page shows the re-filing). Entries here move a store row back to its original where a revision had been written into it.

2026-09-24 (§151, USER RULE 'exclude DR shares like Screener'): 189 new-format rows / 19 symbols where the stored FII was the Institutions (Foreign) bucket TOTAL, i.e. included the 'Overseas Depositories (holding DRs)' custodian line. Each entry = the same row with fii minus that line, read from the same BSE XBRL by the patched parser (src names the file and both figures). The parser now excludes the line (MEMBERS 'od'); guard_shp_definition.py keeps it that way.

2026-09-24 (§152): the SW-2 foreign-block heals re-asserted on 22 rows the store had lost — 20 §142k/date entries updated in place (their `cell` had put the RAW original back over the healed reading) and 2 rows the SW-2 apply had skipped because an unrelated entry already existed. Re-filings now inherit these heals in the fetcher (heal_refiling) instead of undoing them in shp_revisions.json.

2026-09-24 (§153): 13 rows whose stored date was a BSE re-filing date healed to the ORIGINAL filing (values + calendar day) read from BSE's original XBRL; the re-filing values moved to shp_revisions.json (0 rows).

2026-09-24 (§156): the SW-2 sweep's 1,543 unresolved Any-Other cells re-read from BSE's XBRL — 262 cells / 83 symbols where the row holds holders LABELLED foreign (curated name_verdicts or the FII/FPI/Foreign-*/OCB label class) moved dii -> fii by the labelled portion (share counts on the filer's base); e.g. RELIANCE 2016-17 'Foreign Institutional Investors' 12.07/8.55/5.99/2.53 pp. 256 new entries, 6 existing date entries updated in place.

2026-09-24 (§156): new `drop` map = sanctioned retraction of a stored cell while it still equals `was` (apply_cell_fix); first use: the 6 Trendlyne seam cells whose unlabelled Any-Other row hid the legacy FII registrations.

2026-09-24 (§157): 42 §156 entries REVERTED to the pre-heal reading — company/individual-type labels (Foreign/Overseas Corporate Bodies, Foreign Companies, Foreign Nationals) and curated funds nested under them are placed by the 2022 form under Non-Institutions or FDI depending on the filer (UTIAMC T. Rowe Price = Foreign Companies 22.97; IDFCFIRSTB's foreign corporate holder = FDI); handed to the row-level 2022-placement pass (DII session) rather than guessed here.
_doc_bulk_stamp: 2026-08-13: 441 rows across 57 symbols carried ONE identical submission date across >=3 quarters — a scrape date, not a filing date. Separated from the 268 symbols whose late dates are DISTINCT per quarter (genuinely late filers: TALWALKARS, MANPASAND et al) — those are left alone, because for a distressed company a multi-year filing lag is real. The discriminator is the identical-date collapse, and the fii/dii values under it differ per quarter, which is what proves the data was read per-quarter and only the date was stamped.

DSKULKARNI.2023-09-30: Post-insolvency capital reduction: prom steps 46.84 -> 95.00 and STAYS there through 2026-06-30, including later filings with a normal holder count (4,582). The holdings are corroborated; only the nsh=8 is doubtful and it has NOT been verified against BSE.

FEDDERELEC.2021-12-31: prom 100.00 / 7 holders persists across every filing from 2021-12 to 2025-03 and never recovers — consistent with a post-insolvency reduction rather than a one-off wrong document. NOT verified against BSE (symbol absent from bse_scrips by_id).

JPINFRATEC.2024-06-30: Post-resolution (Suraksha): existing equity extinguished, company wholly owned by the resolution applicant. prom 100.00 / 1 holder is the real pattern, not a stub — it persists in every later filing.

2021-09-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 247d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. 2020-09-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 540d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2019-12-31.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2019-12-31.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 961d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2022-09-30.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2022-09-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 738d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2019-09-30.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2019-09-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 389d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2019-09-30.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2019-09-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 666d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2019-09-30.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2019-09-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 234d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2024-03-31.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2024-03-31.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 256d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2022-09-30.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2022-09-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 510d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2024-06-30.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2024-06-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 220d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2019-09-30.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2019-09-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 388d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.

2016-09-30.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2016-09-30.why: WITHIN-SYMBOL OUTLIER: this symbol's own median filing lag is inside the 21-day window, yet this row is 206d late. An otherwise-compliant filer does not file one quarter months late and resume on time. Corrected only because the stamp signature is present as well — the date is shared with another quarter of the same symbol, or the lag exceeds a year. Rows 120-365d late carrying a LONE date are left alone: there a single genuinely-delayed filing cannot be told from a stamp.
2016-09-30.retired: §142g 2026-09-22 orphan re-adjudication: store holds the same filing at share-count precision (4dp); the entry only re-stamped the date and the store's date already equals it — superseded by the §22j precision pass

2023-06-30.src: shp filing-date convention QE+21d (SEBI Reg 31 deadline)
2023-06-30.why: BULK STAMP: 3 quarters of this symbol all carry the single submission date 2025-02-13, which is 594 days after this quarter ended.
